issue.title: USB-002: portable fail-closed transport epoch policy (no IRQ bridge yet)
issue.body:
Owner Dot A personally, independent Critic-A. Next bounded component after USB001 issue46. Scope new firmware/transport/mt_usb_epoch.c/.h, scoped docs and native/ARM tests only; no upstream/host/IRQ implementation changes in this iteration.

Motivation: real unchanged TinyUSB counterexamples reproduce lost reset on full queue, stale-completion rearm and lost SETUP accounting. A linker wrapper alone is insufficient. This task implements only the deterministic epoch/permission policy needed by a later explicit core bridge, not that bridge itself.

Result: nonzero non-reused hard epochs; reset observed before queue outcome; only successfully enqueued then processed current reset permits enumeration after explicit foreground cleanup acknowledgment; current-epoch configuration permits app I/O, sticky soft pause requires explicit resolution; any current enqueue/submission/completion failure poisons epoch until a later real reset. Old tokens cannot change/poison/reopen newer epoch. Counter exhaustion fails closed; diagnostics saturate without wrap. Caller provides serialization/target critical sections; no volatile-as-lock or hardware claims.

Mandatory verification: transition/reference-model tests, stale token and reordered/duplicate outcomes, queue-loss and later-reset recovery, config-before-reset rejection, soft vs hard boundaries, failures after configuration, epoch saturation, strict C11/sanitizers/ARM ABI. Existing producer/fake-DCD counterexamples remain negative evidence until future hook integration. Target PRIMASK/IRQ implementation, queue-envelope patch, SETUP accounting, DCD guarded calls, automatic reopen and physical timing stay open. Draft only; no merge or assertion of complete USB lifecycle.
